report:
Short answer
Model B was fine-tuned to be an instruction‑following / formatting assistant (human-preference / instruction tuning, with safety/refusal behavior). Concretely: the finetune taught the model to start completions with directive, list‑oriented, short/transformational outputs (mapping/one‑line answers), and to prefer “safe”/refusal-type tokens when appropriate.

Why I conclude that (evidence → interpretation)
- Signal concentrated on early residual positions (very large L2 at pos0 across many middle & late layers).
  - Interpretation: the finetune mostly changes how the model begins a completion (a “system style” or initial-response bias). That is exactly what instruction or assistant fine‑tuning does: shift the model’s starting residual so it generates in an assistant-like style from the first token.
- Patchscope readouts (difference vector injected into an identity prompt) produce short, listy, transformation-style outputs:
  - Many samples are mappings and short structured outputs: “A -> A”, “1000 -> 001000”, repeated pairs, enumerated lists, small-line outputs, short code-like snippets, “print("hello")”, etc.
  - Interpretation: the model has learned to produce concise, formatted, task-oriented answers and to perform simple transformations / normalization tasks. Those are characteristic artifacts of instruction-tuning datasets (lots of explicit tasks, mapping examples, formatting examples).
- Logit‑lens tokens at high‑norm cells move toward instruction/refusal/label words in later layers:
  - Middle-to-late layers’ top tokens include verbs and directives (“Do”, “Check”, “prepare”, “ensure”, “strive”), framing words (“Every”, “Stay”, “consider”, “recommend”), and refusal/safety/assessment words (“rejected”, “relevant”, “normal”, “damaged”, “tragic”, “law”, “surgeon”, “clinic”).
  - Interpretation: the change biases the vocabulary the model is likely to produce at the start toward instruction words, evaluative or safety tokens, and short answer connectors — again consistent with assistant-style fine-tuning that emphasizes helpful directives and safe refusals/labels.
- Evolution of token themes across layers
  - Early-layer top tokens (pos0) include lots of ordinary content words (bottle, wings,Author) but later/larger cells shift to instruction/refusal/evaluative tokens. This matches how style/intent tends to be injected later in the network and at the start token for instruction-tuned models.
- Mixed domain words (surgeon, clinic, tragic, law, volunteers, rescue, downturn) suggest the finetune included many safety/harmlessness or real-world-labeling examples (news/incident descriptions and a need to label/respond safely), which explains the presence of “rejected/tragic/rescue” vocabulary in high-norm cells.

Summary statement
All three diagnostics point to a finetune that changes the model’s initial-residual so it reliably begins completions in a compact, task-oriented, instruction-following style (with learned refusal/safety/evaluative behaviors). In short: Model B = Model A + instruction/RLHF-style assistant tuning (emphasising concise, list/transform/label outputs and safer/refusal wording).
